title: Sales Tax Basis on Kept Total-Loss Vehicles, Cardinal Physical Damage Coverage
content:
**Rule.** On a total-loss vehicle the customer keeps under Cardinal Physical Damage Coverage, where a vehicle has been added to the Cardinal Personal Auto Policy with an effective date after the loss date, the customer has bought a replacement and the kept-vehicle sales tax is figured on the full kept value; where no vehicle has been added since the loss and fewer than 30 days have passed from the loss date to the acceptance date, no kept-vehicle sales tax is paid with the settlement; otherwise the kept-vehicle sales tax is figured on the kept value less the salvage deduction.

Vehicle additions are the vehicle-add transactions on the Cardinal Personal Auto Policy; a vehicle added with an effective date on the loss date itself is not added after it. The loss date is read from the claim's loss report.

## Basis questions and answers (hypothetical figures: KY policy, 6.00 percent; kept value 11700.00; salvage deduction 2500.00)

**A replacement car was added to the policy two weeks after the loss.** Tax on the full kept value: 6.00 percent of 11700.00 gives 702.00.

**No vehicle has been added, and the settlement is accepted 29 days after the loss.** Fewer than 30 days: no kept-vehicle sales tax is paid with the settlement.

**No vehicle has been added, accepted 30 days after the loss.** Not fewer than 30 days: tax on 11700.00 less 2500.00, that is 9200.00, giving 552.00.

| Vehicle added with effective date after the loss | Days from loss to acceptance | Tax figured on |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | Any | Full kept value |
| No | Fewer than 30 | No kept-vehicle sales tax |
| No | 30 or more | Kept value less the salvage deduction |
